as_written_in_papers.quote: Sequencing of ALDH5A1 revealed a heterozygous splice site variant c.610-612A>G (IVS3-2A>G) in intron 3, and a heterozygous missense mutation c.1333A>C (p.M445L) in exon 9.

cases.statement: One person: a girl with early-onset SSADH deficiency, heterozygous for the splice variant written c.610-612A>G (IVS3-2A>G) and for c.1333A>C (p.M445L); biparental inheritance stated.

people.label: patient
people.zygosity_or_genotype: heterozygous for each of two variants; biparental inheritance stated (compound heterozygous)
people.key_phenotypes: stiffening episodes from 1.5 months; hypotonia and head lag; exaggerated Moro and startle response; hyporeflexia; marked urinary 4-hydroxybutyric acid elevation

quotes.quote: Sequencing of ALDH5A1 revealed a heterozygous splice site variant c.610-612A>G (IVS3-2A>G) in intron 3, and a heterozygous missense mutation c.1333A>C (p.M445L) in exon 9.
At 1.5 months of age, she developed stiffening episodes characterized by appearance of holding her breath, appearing startled, and arm extension.

On examination at 1.5 months of age she had hypotonia, head lag, a stiffening episode lasting for seconds, some downward inner movement of the eyes at that point, and an exaggerated Moro reflex and startle response.
Deep tendon reflexes were preserved at first evaluation at 1.5 months of age but hyporeflexia was present thereafter.

Urine organic acids showed a marked elevation of 4-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB) as well as abnormal elevations of 4,5-dihydroxyhexanoic acid lactones, glycolic, 3-hydroxypropionic, glutaric, adipic, and 2-hydroxyglutaric acids consistent with the diagnosis of SSADH deficiency.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Urine organic acids showed a marked GHB elevation, which the authors call consistent with SSADH deficiency; several other metabolic and laboratory tests were normal, and brain MRI was normal. No other genes were reported as tested.

quotes.quote: Urine organic acids showed a marked elevation of 4-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB) as well as abnormal elevations of 4,5-dihydroxyhexanoic acid lactones, glycolic, 3-hydroxypropionic, glutaric, adipic, and 2-hydroxyglutaric acids consistent with the diagnosis of SSADH deficiency.
Plasma amino acids, plasma total and free carnitine, plasma acylcarnitine profile, creatine kinase, electrolytes, complete blood count, lactate, and thyroid function tests were normal.
Brain MRI at age 4 months was normal and has not been repeated.
We report a patient with an early-onset SSADH deficiency with low GSH levels in blood suggesting increased oxidative stress.

segregation.statement: Only the statement that biparental inheritance was confirmed; which parent carries which variant and the parents' status are not given. Parents are non-consanguineous.

quotes.quote: The patient was born after an uncomplicated pregnancy to non-consanguineous parents via cesarean section due to prolonged labor.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo by the paper's account: biparental inheritance is stated (no per-parent details).

in_trans.statement: Other allele c.1333A>C (p.M445L). Phase is stated as confirmed by biparental inheritance; per-parent genotypes are not given.

quotes.quote: Sequencing of ALDH5A1 revealed a heterozygous splice site variant c.610-612A>G (IVS3-2A>G) in intron 3, and a heterozygous missense mutation c.1333A>C (p.M445L) in exon 9.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Described by the authors as a splice-site variant at the acceptor (-2) position of intron 3 (IVS3-2A>G); no protein consequence stated. The batch HGVS c.610-612T>G places it 612 bases into the intron instead (see concerns). The paper states only that the disease is caused by ALDH5A1 mutations.

quotes.quote: Sequencing of ALDH5A1 revealed a heterozygous splice site variant c.610-612A>G (IVS3-2A>G) in intron 3, and a heterozygous missense mutation c.1333A>C (p.M445L) in exon 9.
is a rare disorder (OMIM 271980) of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) degradation caused by mutations in ALDH5A1[1], [2].

computational_predictions.statement: not reported in 27896081. (37503297/37962671 give SpliceAI 0.96 loss / 0.44 gain for "c.610–2A > G"; whether that is this variant is unresolved, see concerns.)

authors_classification.statement: Authors state both variants were previously reported (refs 8 and 21) and give their own classification.

quotes.quote: Both mutations have been previously reported [8], [21] and are considered pathogenic.

concerns: Major numbering problem. The paper writes "c.610-612A>G (IVS3-2A>G)". "c.610-612" is not a standard position; the legacy name IVS3-2A>G points to the -2 acceptor position before exon 4 (c.610-2). The batch HGVS NM_001080.3:c.610-612T>G (VCF 6:24504257:T:G) appears to read the string literally as 612 bases upstream, and its reference base (T) disagrees with the paper's stated reference base (A). The batch coordinate is probably not the variant the authors meant; the panel should resolve the variant identity first.

If the intended variant is c.610-2A>G, it is not a new variant within this batch: 37503297/37962671 Table 2 #48 carries "c.610–2A > G" with "c.1294A > C" (M432L). That person is not linked to this candidate in the batch.

Possible same genotype under different numbering: this patient's other allele is c.1333A>C (p.M445L), while 37503297 #48 has c.1294A>C (M432L); the two differ by exactly 39 nucleotides / 13 residues, consistent with an alternative-transcript or legacy numbering. The papers do not say whether these are the same variant or the same person (this patient was reported at age 10 months in 2014; the cohort study began in 2018).
Exon/intron numbering differs between papers: 27896081 places the splice variant in intron 3, 37503297 places c.610–2A > G in intron 4.
No transcript is stated in 27896081, and c.1333A>C (p.M445L) may itself use legacy numbering.
